header.name: Bayesian Machine Learning
header.description: In this course, we will discuss the foundations of Bayesian statistical modeling in the context of machine learning through various case-studies/running-examples. Some of the key benefits of the Bayesian approach include the ability to quantify the uncertainty in the parameters/predictions through posterior probability distributions, the ability to incorporate prior knowledge in a principled way, the ability to learn the model hyperparameters and the right model size/complexity automatically from data. This course will provide a platform to set up a machine learning problem as a Bayesian model and design exact or approximate (sampling/optimization) solution methods for computationally scalable inference. This course provides foundations to modern methods of Bayesian modelling.

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: Explain and summarise the differences between point estimation and Bayesian approaches.

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: Explain the Bayesian counterparts of existing machine learning techniques.

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: Analyse and implement approximate inference techniques.

outcomes.label: CO4
outcomes.raw_text: Develop skills to analyse research problems using Bayesian methods.

outcomes.label: CO5
outcomes.raw_text: Explain the scalability issues and implement solutions using Bayesian algorithms.

Bayesian Inference with (Point) Estimation of Hyperparameters
